This Camper Van Is a Warm Mobile Abode Built for Year-Round Comfort Wherever the Road Leads
22 photos
Photo: Vantra
In the case of some camper vans, it's not an exaggeration to call them homes on wheels – they can be as comfortable as a simple studio apartment, but a lot more practical. Take the rig I'd like to share with you today as an example.
What we have here is a project based on a 2026 Ford Transit with a 148" wheelbase, a high roof, and an AWD drivetrain. It was professionally built by Vantra, a Wilmington, North Carolina-based company that specializes in custom Ram ProMaster and Ford Transit AWD camper vans.
As always, let's begin the tour with the exterior. First off, the van rides on black Method wheels wrapped in Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires.
At the rear, you'll come across a spare tire carrier / ladder combo. Use it to climb on top of the van, and you'll discover a powder-coated aluminum roof rack holding a Fiamma manual awning and two 200 W solar panels.
Like a lot of premium mobile homes, this van sports a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's flares are paint matched to the van's body and come with windows with sliding screens.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vantra Stepping inside, a warm and well-crafted interior will greet you. Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for grey woven vinyl flooring, a slatted cedar ceiling, and cabinetry with bamboo faces. The look is complemented by white Corian solid surface countertops and some black accents, like the kitchen hardware or the cabinet and drawer handles.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've set up camp. This simple seating setup is completed by a Lagun table.
The first part of the living space is the kitchen positioned dead ahead of the entrance. It features a deep black stainless steel sink, a 115-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a portable induction stove. Moreover, a vent fan above will help draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Two overhead cabinets, a small drawer, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter hides a 4-gallon (15-liter) electric water heater and a single-stage water filtration system.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vantra Next, we have a bench with a Lagun table on the opposite side, by the entrance. If you lift the bench's hinged top, you'll reveal some storage space. There's more than meets the eye here – this compartment has a false bottom that hides a heater underneath.
Despite the limited interior real estate, Vantra found the space to install a Van Wife Components shower stall. It's made from powder-coated aluminum and measures 24 x 24 inches (61 x 61 centimeters). It houses a shower with a removable sprayer and a portable toilet.
Just like in most camper vans, the rear part of the living space is reserved for sleeping. The bedroom offers a 6-inch-thick, queen-size memory foam mattress and two upper cabinets.
Your bulkiest items will most likely fit in the van's garage, which is underneath the bedroom. It's accessible directly from the living space or through the back of the van, after opening the rear doors.
Photo: Vantra
Besides offering a bunch of room for storage in its middle part, the garage has two tall boxes on the sides that hold the bed platform and accommodate part of the utility systems.
Power is on the right side – the rig's electrical heart is a 10 kWh Bluetti RV5 system. It can be charged via three sources: shore power, solar power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running thanks to an alternator charger. If you use these correctly and efficiently, you might never run out of juice while on the road.
On plumbing, the van is equipped with a 24-gallon (94-liter) freshwater tank, a 22-gallon (83-liter) greywater tank, a 4-gallon (15-liter) water heater, and an outdoor shower connection.
This van was built for year-round comfort, regardless of where you travel. Two systems make the rig four-season-capable: a 48V Velit A/C unit and a gas-powered Velit 12V heater. Moreover, the builders added 3M Thinsulate insulation and sound deadening throughout the van.
Photo: Vantra The "command center" for the utility systems is conveniently located above the entrance. It includes a large touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power and water systems, a thermostat, and dimmer switches for four lighting zones.
All in all, this fully-equipped Transit camper van by Vantra is not only designed to keep going long after the pavement ends, but it also keeps you nice and comfortable regardless of where and when you travel.
